protocol_before_daily_outcomes:
# MAX persistent reaction tails — prospective specification for retrospective extraction

Recorded before inspecting daily outcomes, 2026-09-28. User-nominated examples:
MSU Lomonosov, MIPT, Kuindzhi, Southwest State, Kursk State. These are case-study
identities, never fraud/organic labels. Screenshots show MAX and a partial Sep24
day; full daily analysis must not claim an exact reproduction of their values.

H18: repeated late reaction breadth differs across MAX accounts after accounting
for age, view opportunity, early reaction propensity, posting rate and observation
coverage. H19: a long smoothly decreasing tail alone identifies manipulation
(seek a counterexample, not assume the claim). H20: the difference survives
conditioning on baseline ER and view increments; H21: limited M0 selection can
support an unbiased 4–14 day tail test (audit the existing age and selection cap).

Frame: all nondeleted MAX accounts with >=15 original nondeleted posts in
Aug31–Sep27 UTC, selected by publication counts only; include nominated accounts.
Daily window Sep14–27 Moscow, freeze input before Sep28 00:00 UTC. Each selected
account is queried separately, read only, statement timeout 60s. All publications
Aug30 21:00 UTC–Sep27 21:00 UTC, originals main and reposts sensitivity.
Extract only last observed endpoints for each Moscow day Sep13–27 plus
pre-24h endpoint, with correction lineage. Keep NULL/missing/uncertain/negative
as such. No interpolation or account-log zero fill. Primary daily endpoints
must both be exact, not uncertain, <=3h stale at midnight; sensitivity <=1h and
<=6h; elapsed interval 18–30h. Post age at interval start >=1d for comparable
full days. Bins 1–2,2–4,4–7,7–14 days; late means start age >=4 and end age <=14.

Report raw daily and pooled coverage, positive late reaction fraction, late
reaction share, reactions per 1000 additional views, late/early reaction-to-view
ratio, adjusted breadth from count expectation, day-by-day repetition, cohort
ranks without certified p-values. Normalize by number of eligible observed
posts. Do not count recurrent days as independent replications. Label all
results exploratory; cohort is not independently verified organic.

Models: simple log-link count models with view exposure and baseline reaction
ratio; compare shared age curve vs account-specific aging, posting frequency
and feed depth using chronological fit Sep14–20 / test Sep21–27. Estimate NB2
dispersion on fit only. If insufficient eligible observations, report abstention.
Evaluate test count deviance/MAE, not train fit as evidence; case deletion and
leave-account-out peer curves for sensitivity. Baseline cumulative ER at 24h is
a covariate, not a trusted organic label; exclude future-informed baseline use.

Construct conventional decaying exposure + count-response scenarios to test
whether long repeated graded tails can arise without organized intervention;
compare alternative generation with equal observables. Assess coupled growth
and randomized late additions only as sensitivity, never empirical fraud recall.
protocol_implementation_notes: H22 conditional allocation is post-hoc; exploratory only
Negative-binomial held-out log likelihood used, rather than a fitted deviance proxy
Peer fit excludes the five nominated cases jointly; this is not full leave-one-account-out validation
Coupled smooth-addition and lag simulations H13-H17 are not completed in this cycle
Same posts can cross calendar train/test split; only conditional future-interval evaluation
